requirements.requirement: Nginx backends on node1, node2, and node3 serve their respective node identifiers from `/` on port 5660.
requirements.summary: Final checks show valid Nginx configurations, active and enabled services, listeners on 0.0.0.0:5660, and HTTP 200 responses containing node1, node2, and node3 respectively.

requirements.requirement: HAProxy on node4 serves HTTP on port 80 and distributes requests across the healthy backends.
requirements.summary: HAProxy had a valid configuration, was active and enabled, listened on 0.0.0.0:80, and repeated HTTP 200 requests rotated evenly across all three backends at baseline and in the final state.

requirements.requirement: The HTTP service remains available through the failure of any single backend and returns to full operation after recovery.
requirements.summary: A complete transition was observed for node2: all backends served traffic at baseline; node2 was stopped and its listener and direct HTTP service became unavailable; 12 of 12 HAProxy requests still returned HTTP 200 through node1 and node3; node2 was restarted; and subsequent traffic succeeded through all three backends.

overall_summary: All material functional outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates correct backend responses, HAProxy distribution, a bounded backend outage with uninterrupted service, restoration, and reintegration. Only operational cleanup and unnecessary backend port-80 exposure detract from the result.
limitations: Only node2 was directly disrupted; node1 and node3 failure cases were not individually exercised, although the symmetric HAProxy configuration and successful node2 transition support the single-failure outcome.
HAProxy requests were issued locally on node4 using its node address rather than from a separate client node.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required services ended healthy, with no captured failed units or package-manager inconsistency. Hygiene is reduced because executor-created candidate, response, installation log, PID, and completion files remained under `/tmp` on every node, and the default Nginx configuration also exposed unnecessary port-80 listeners on node1, node2, and node3 in addition to the required port 5660.
